content:
Key observations from test image:
- Soybean stems remain **green** while the pods are already tan/brown and mature/dried
- Pods appear shriveled or underdeveloped
- Classic presentation of stem staying green while rest of plant matures

This strongly suggests **Green_stem_disorder**. Let me confirm with reference images.
The Green_stem_disorder reference is an excellent match — top-right panel shows nearly identical: green stems with tan dried pods against dark soil background.

Neither Sudden_death_syndrome (leaf interveinal chlorosis) nor Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus (leaf mottling, beetles) match. The comparison confirms my diagnosis.

**Analysis summary:**
- **Test image**: Green soybean stems persisting with tan/brown dried, shriveled pods — the plant failed to mature normally, stem stayed physiologically green while pods dried
- **Green_stem_disorder reference**: Top-right panel is nearly identical — green stems, tan dried pods, dark soil background
- **Ruled out**: Phomopsis (pod lesions/spots), Charcoal_Rot (bleached stems/root rot), Diaporthe (stem cankers), Sudden_death_syndrome (leaf necrosis), Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus (leaf mottling)
